applies_to: G3 per-ID comparison, Build B (B sources in the worktree) vs Build E (E sources), CPU run and GPU lines alike, same pytest options
default: every test ID has the identical outcome (passed/failed/skipped/error/xfailed/xpassed) on both builds; collection errors identical by file; any other difference is a regression

intended.allowed: passed -> failed (or error), only when the Build E failure text names tensor_cuda/src/kernels.cu or tensor_cuda/src/bindings.cpp
intended.ruling: a byte/sha pin of a source file this round edits (kernels.cu core section, bindings.cpp A1.1 hooks and A2.1 Bool branch) moved because of that edit; L38 forbids changing the existing test, so the moved pin is listed, not re-pinned. Files: the suite files that read kernels.cu/bindings.cpp/core.h (grep), core.h is unchanged.

intended.allowed: failed -> passed, only when the Build B failure text is a host-path CUDA failure of an E2 member ('CUDA error at from_host' / 'CUDA error at to_host' / 'CUDA error at astype' on a host tensor, or an HMM fault)
intended.ruling: E2: the host paths no longer need a device (HOST-TENSOR-NEEDS-DEVICE, HOST-ASTYPE-HMM). Build B CPU run cpu_B_srcE showed no such failure text, so none is expected.

intended.ids_reading_bool_numpy: test_eng2.py rows with dtype bool that call _host_bytes (it slices the first numel bytes of the old float32 buffer); test_eng3's own G1b rows are not in the suite
intended.allowed: failed -> passed; passed -> passed (predicted: test_eng2's _host_bytes reads the first numel bytes, which are the same bytes under both outputs)
intended.ruling: A2.2: bool .numpy() changes from a float32 garbage array to the correct bool array; any test that relied on the old output is listed here
